22 When a guitar string is plucked, it causes a longitudinal sound wave in the air, as shown.

The speed of sound in the air is 340 m s–1.
What is the approximate frequency of the sound wave shown?
A
430 Hz
B
680 Hz
C
1100 Hz
D
1400 Hz

hints: Look at where the dots are most crowded in the distance plot from 0.0 m to 0.8 m - the dense regions near 0.0 m and near 0.5 m are successive compressions.
Recall that for a longitudinal wave one wavelength is the distance from the centre of one compression to the centre of the next compression.
Connect the estimated wavelength of about $0.5 \text{ m}$ to $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $f$.
walkthrough: Identify the compressions on the dot diagram: maximum dot density is near distance $0.0 \text{ m}$ and again near distance $0.5 \text{ m}$.
State the rule for wavelength: $\lambda$ is the distance between equivalent points, so centre of one compression to centre of the next compression.
Estimate $\lambda \approx 0.5 - 0.0 = 0.5 \text{ m}$ from the scale, noting the sparse rarefaction is between them near $0.25 \text{ m}$.
Use the wave equation $v = f\lambda$ rearranged to $f = v/\lambda$.
Substitute $v = 340 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $\lambda \approx 0.5 \text{ m}$ to get $f \approx 340/0.5 = 680 \text{ Hz}$, with unit $\text{Hz}$ as $\text{s}^{-1}$.

A.explanation: Gives $f \approx 430 \text{ Hz}$ if $\lambda \approx 0.8 \text{ m}$ is used, which treats the whole 0.0 to 0.8 m diagram as one wavelength instead of the compression to compression distance.

B.explanation: Uses $\lambda \approx 0.5 \text{ m}$ between adjacent compressions with $f = v/\lambda = 340/0.5 \approx 680 \text{ Hz}$.

C.explanation: Gives too high a frequency because it uses too short a wavelength of about $0.3 \text{ m}$, for example the distance from a compression to the next rarefaction.

D.explanation: Gives about double the correct frequency because it uses $\lambda \approx 0.25 \text{ m}$, about half the true compression to compression distance.
